articles.summary: Veo 3.1 holds a character through Ingredients to Video: supply up to three reference images of your character, prompt the action, and reuse the same references on every shot. Chain clips with scene extension to keep the identity across a longer sequence.

articles.summary: Midjourney locks a character's identity through Omni Reference: the --oref parameter, tuned with omni-weight (--ow). Supply a reference image, keep the weight balanced, and your character holds from shot to shot.

articles.summary: GPT Image has no saved-character feature, so consistency comes from method: keep every generation in one chat thread, re-feed your reference image, and re-anchor on the best output. It holds a look across a session but drifts over time.
articles.title: How to Keep a Character Consistent in GPT Image

articles.summary: Nano Banana, Google's Gemini image model, is praised for character consistency: supply reference images of your subject and edit conversationally to place the same face in new scenes. Nano Banana Pro blends up to fourteen references and holds up to five subjects.
articles.title: How to Keep a Character Consistent in Nano Banana

articles.summary: ComfyUI holds a character by stacking nodes: an IPAdapter FaceID adapter for identity, ControlNet for pose, and a FaceDetailer pass to sharpen the face. No training needed, but it takes a careful graph and a capable GPU.
articles.title: How to Keep a Character Consistent in ComfyUI
